subject.title: fix(cli): oversized secrets plans consume unbounded memory

question: Should saved secrets plans become a hard 16 MiB public CLI contract, rejecting previously accepted larger hand-written and externally generated plans?
rationale: The resource-exhaustion fix is sound, but selecting and shipping a fixed ceiling intentionally changes an existing CLI input contract and requires maintainer ownership rather than reviewer inference.

options.title: Accept the 16 MiB contract
options.body: Ship the documented ceiling because normal plans are far smaller and the matching configure/apply checks prevent incompatible generated artifacts.

options.title: Choose another fixed ceiling
options.body: Adjust the constant, help text, documentation, proof, and boundary tests together before merge if operators plausibly need larger serialized plans.

recommendation.title: Accept the 16 MiB contract
recommendation.body: Ship the documented ceiling because normal plans are far smaller and the matching configure/apply checks prevent incompatible generated artifacts.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects steipete to the canonical secrets contract and releases carrying adjacent secrets behavior.
